title: I Can, I Like
overview: Say what you can do and what you can't do. Ask: Can you swim? Say what you like, love and hate: I like cooking. Join two things with and.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 26 words.
Patterns: 3 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Say them.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about you. Made-up answers are OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 4.
In this unit, you say what you can do.
And you say what you like.
Listen.
I can cook. I can drive.
I can't swim.
Can: yes. Can't: no.
Can't and cannot are the same.
After can, the word stays the same.
I can swim. Not: I can swimming.
He can sing. She can dance. Can has no s.
Now a question.
Can you swim?
Yes, I can. No, I can't.
Listen to can and can't.
Can is short. Can't is long.
I can swim. I can't swim.
Now like.
I like music.
I like cooking.
After like, add -ing: cook, cooking.
Love: like it very, very much. I love dancing.
Don't like is no. I don't like running.
Hate is no, not at all. I hate running.
Look at dancing. Dance ends in e. Drop the e.
Look at running and swimming. Two n. Two m.
Now and.
And is for two things.
Music and films.
I can cook and I can drive.
Three things? I can sing, dance and draw.
After like, both words take -ing.
I like cooking and swimming.
Now you. Say one thing you can do.
Say one thing you like.
It can be true or made up.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

words.meaning: Move in water with your arms and legs.
practice: Can you swim? Yes, I can.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for six short lines with can or like and a gap. Fill each gap: swim after can, swimming after like.

words.meaning: Make food hot, to eat.
practice: Can you cook? Yes, I can.
words.tutor: Say I like cooking, then I don't like cooking, to the tutor. Ask it which line says yes and which says no.

words.meaning: Make a car or a bus go.
practice: Can you drive? No, I can't.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor Can you drive? and listen to its answer. Then answer the same question for you. True or made up is fine.

words.meaning: Say words to music, like a song.
words.tutor: Sing or say one line of any song to the tutor. Then tell it I can sing, or I can't sing.

words.meaning: Move your body to music.
words.tutor: Type dancing for the tutor. Ask it to check you dropped the e: dancing, not danceing.

words.meaning: Make a picture with a pen or a pencil.
words.tutor: Draw a small picture on paper. Tell the tutor I can draw a … and name it. Ask it for any word you need.

words.meaning: Go on your legs, not fast.
practice: I can walk to the bus stop.
words.tutor: Say walk five times to the tutor. Ask it if the l was quiet each time, as it should be.

words.meaning: Go on your legs, fast.
practice: Can you run to the bus?
words.tutor: Type running for the tutor and ask it to check the two n in the middle.

words.meaning: Sit on a bike and make it go.
practice: Ivan can ride a bike and drive a bus.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor I can ride a bike or I can't ride a bike. Then ask the tutor the same: Can you ride a bike?

words.meaning: Do a game, or make music.
words.tutor: Name two games you can play, real or made up. Say them to the tutor as one line: I can play … and … .

words.meaning: Say words. People speak a language.
practice: Can you speak English? Yes, I can.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor I can speak English and one more thing you can do, as one line with and.

words.meaning: Say numbers in order: one, two, three.
words.tutor: Count from one to twenty with the tutor, taking turns. Then say I can count to twenty.

words.meaning: Take a thing in your hands and walk with it.
practice: The box is big. I can't carry it.
Please carry the chair to the door.
words.tutor: Look round the room. Tell the tutor two things you can carry and one big thing you can't carry.

words.meaning: Rest in bed with your eyes closed.
practice: I can't sleep. It is hot.
The baby is in bed. Sleep, baby!
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you love doing and one thing you hate doing. Put sleeping in one of them.

words.meaning: A game. Two teams play with one ball.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor Can you play football? Then answer the same question. Your answer can be true or made up.

words.meaning: Songs and sounds you listen to.
practice: My music is on my phone.
We can sing and dance to music.
Music, films and games: I like them.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three free-time words. Answer each with I like, I love or I don't like. Put music in one.

words.meaning: It has got two wheels. You ride it.
practice: The bike is next to the door.
I have got a new bike.
This is my bike. It is blue.
words.tutor: Describe a bike to the tutor, real or made up, with two describing words and and: My bike is … and … .

words.meaning: A thing you play, like football or cards.
practice: The game is on my phone.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor What is your favourite game? Then answer the same question. Any game is fine.

words.meaning: Words and music. You sing it.
practice: I can sing two songs in English.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor a favourite song, real or made up. Say one word from it and ask the tutor to spell it for you.

words.meaning: A long story you look at, on TV or a big screen.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a film you like: its name and one describing word, like long or new. A made-up film is fine.

words.meaning: A screen at home. Films and games are on it.
words.example: The TV is on the wall.
practice: The TV is big and new.
Is the TV on the table?
words.tutor: Say where a TV is in a room, real or made up, with on, in, near or next to.

words.meaning: Like a thing very, very much.
practice: I like cooking. I love dancing.
Like is good. Love is very, very good.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three lines in order: I love …, I like … and I don't like … . Ask it to check the -ing words.

words.meaning: Not like a thing at all.
practice: I don't like it. I hate it!
I love swimming and I hate running.
Hate and hat: hate has an e at the end.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you hate doing, with -ing. True or made up is fine. Ask it to check the spelling.

words.meaning: Your number one: the one you like the most.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three favourites: a colour, a song and a game. Type favourite once and ask the tutor to check the o-u in it.

words.meaning: Words people speak. English is one.
practice: English is a new language for me.
Language: the u comes after the g.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor I can speak … languages, with a number. Any number is fine, true or made up.

words.meaning: The language you read here.
practice: Hello and goodbye are English words.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three English words you like from this unit. Ask it to use each one in a short line for you to repeat.

grammar.title: Can and can't: I can swim, I can't drive
grammar.explanation:
Can: yes. I can cook.
Can't: no. I can't drive.
Can't and cannot are the same.
After can, the word stays the same.
grammar.rule:
I can swim.
You can drive.
He can cook.
She can sing.
We can dance.
They can run.

I can't swim.
She can't drive.

Can you swim?
Yes, I can.
No, I can't.

He can, she can: no s.
Not: he cans.
grammar.workedExample:
Sam: swim, yes. Drive, no.
1. Swim, yes: can.
2. Sam can swim.
3. Drive, no: can't.
4. Sam can't drive.
5. Check: swim and drive stay the same. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to add to or -ing after can.
No: I can to swim.
No: I can swimming.
Yes: I can swim.
grammar.tip: Can, then the word as it is.
grammar.practice:
Write can or can't.
1. Lena: cook, yes. Lena ___ cook.
2. Ivan: drive, no. Ivan ___ drive.
3. Zoe: swim, yes. Zoe ___ swim.
4. Yara: sing, no. Yara ___ sing.
5. Tomas: ride a bike, yes. Tomas ___ ride a bike.
6. Mia: draw, no. Mia ___ draw.
7. ___ you swim? Yes, I can.
8. Can you drive? No, I ___.
grammar.answers:
1. can  2. can't  3. can  4. can't  5. can  6. can't  7. Can  8. can't
Wrong on 7? A question starts with Can: Can you swim?
Wrong on 8? No goes with can't: No, I can't.

grammar.title: Like with -ing: I like singing
grammar.explanation:
Say what you like and do not like.
Use like, love, don't like or hate.
Then a thing, or a word with -ing.
I like music. I like cooking.
grammar.rule:
I love dancing.
I like cooking.
I don't like running.
I hate carrying bags.

a thing: I like music.
a word with -ing: I like singing.

Make the -ing word:
cook, cooking
sing, singing
carry, carrying

An e at the end? Drop the e.
dance, dancing
drive, driving
ride, riding

swim, swimming: two m
run, running: two n
grammar.workedExample:
Dance: yes, very, very much. Write a line.
1. Very, very much: love.
2. After love: a word with -ing.
3. Dance has an e at the end. Drop the e.
4. dance, dancing.
5. Write: I love dancing.
6. Check: no e before -ing. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out -ing after like.
No: I like cook.
Yes: I like cooking.
No: I like swiming.
Yes: I like swimming. Two m.
grammar.practice:
Write the word with -ing.
1. I like ___. (cook)
2. I love ___. (dance)
3. I don't like ___. (run)
4. I hate ___ bags. (carry)
5. I like ___. (sing)
6. I love ___. (swim)
7. I don't like ___. (drive)
8. I like ___. (draw)
grammar.answers:
1. cooking  2. dancing  3. running  4. carrying  5. singing  6. swimming  7. driving  8. drawing
Wrong on 2 or 7? Dance and drive end in e. Drop the e.
Wrong on 3 or 6? Run and swim take two letters: running, swimming.

grammar.title: And: sing and dance
grammar.explanation:
Use and for two things.
Two words: music and films.
Two parts: I can cook and I can drive.
grammar.rule:
Two words:
Ana and Sam
music and films
sing and dance

Two parts:
I can cook and I can drive.
I like music and I love dancing.

Or say can one time:
I can cook and drive.

Three things? A comma, then and:
I can sing, dance and draw.

After like, both words take -ing:
I like cooking and swimming.
After can, no -ing:
I can cook and swim.
grammar.workedExample:
I can sing. I can dance.
Make one sentence.
1. Two lines, both with I can.
2. Put and in the middle.
3. I can sing and I can dance.
4. Or: I can sing and dance.
5. One full stop, at the end.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to drop -ing after and.
No: I like cooking and swim.
Yes: I like cooking and swimming.
After can, no -ing at all.
No: I can sing and dancing.
Yes: I can sing and dance.
grammar.tip: Two things, one and, one full stop.
grammar.practice:
Make one sentence with and.
1. I can cook. I can drive.
2. I like music. I like films.
3. Ana can swim. Sam can swim.
4. I love singing. I love dancing.
5. I can't swim. I can't drive.
6. I can walk. I can run. I can ride a bike.
grammar.answers:
1. I can cook and I can drive. Or: I can cook and drive.
2. I like music and films. Or: I like music and I like films.
3. Ana and Sam can swim.
4. I love singing and dancing. Or: I love singing and I love dancing.
5. I can't swim and I can't drive.
6. I can walk, run and ride a bike.
Wrong on 6? Three things: a comma, then and.
Wrong on 4? After love, both words take -ing.

readings.title: Three People at a Group
readings.setting: Three people say what they can do and like, at a free-time group.
readings.passage:
I am Lena. I can cook and I can drive. I can't swim. I love cooking.
I am Ivan. I can swim and I can ride a bike. I can't sing. I don't like running.
I am Zoe. I can speak two languages. I can draw. I like drawing and music.

readings.title: Twenty People, Two Questions
readings.setting: A group at a library asks twenty people.
readings.passage:
Twenty people. Two questions.
Can you swim?
12 people can swim. 8 people can't.
Can you drive?
9 people can drive. 11 people can't.
They like:
music: 18 people
films: 15 people
football: 10 people
cooking: 7 people
The favourite is music!

readings.title: A Sign at the Pool
readings.setting: The door of the pool at a sports centre.
readings.passage:
THE POOL
Can you swim? Go to the big pool.
You can't swim? Go to the small pool.
Please walk. No running.
No phones in the pool.
Bikes: next to the door.

comprehension.why: Line 1: I am Lena. I can cook and I can drive.
Line 2: I am Ivan. I can't sing.

comprehension.q: I like drawing. Who can say this?
comprehension.why: Line 3: I am Zoe. I like drawing and music.

comprehension.q: You want a map. Lena, Ivan or Zoe: who can draw it?
comprehension.why: Line 3: I can draw. Lena and Ivan do not say draw.

comprehension.q: 12 people can ___. Which word is it?

comprehension.why: Line 5: 9 people can drive. 11 people can't.

comprehension.a: 18 people like music. It has the big number.
comprehension.why: Music: 18. Films: 15. Football: 10. Cooking: 7. The favourite is the one people like the most.

comprehension.q: You can't swim. Which pool is for you?
comprehension.why: The sign says: You can't swim? Go to the small pool.

comprehension.q: You have got a phone. Can it go in the pool?
comprehension.why: The sign says: No phones in the pool.

comprehension.q: The sign says: No running. So: walk or run?

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — I can, I can't
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
I can cook.
I can't drive.
He can swim.
She can't sing.
Can you dance?
Yes, I can. No, I can't.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: cook, drive, swim, sing, dance. No -ing after can?
speaking.tutor: Say the six lines to the tutor. Ask it to tell you any line with -ing or to after can.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — What you can do
speaking.instructions:
Say 4 lines about you.
I can ___.
I can ___ and ___.
I can't ___.
I can't ___.
Pick from: swim, cook, drive, sing, dance, draw.
It can be true or made up.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 lines? And in line 2? No -ing?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say 4 lines about you.
I can …
I can … and …
I can't …
I can't …
Pick from: swim, cook, drive, sing, dance, draw.
It can be true or made up.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 4 lines? And in line 2? No -ing?
speaking.tutor: Give the tutor your four lines. Ask it to ask you Can you …? about two new things, and answer with Yes, I can or No, I can't.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Can you swim?
speaking.instructions:
Listen to each question. Say your answer.
Can you swim?
Can you cook?
Can you drive?
Can you speak English?
Say: Yes, I can. Or say: No, I can't.
Your answer can be true or made up.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check: yes with can? No with can't?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask you six Can you …? questions in any order. Answer each with Yes, I can or No, I can't, not one word.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Can or can't?
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
I can swim. Can is short.
I can't swim. Can't is long.
I can cook. I can't cook.
I can drive. I can't drive.
The t in can't is quiet.
The long sound says no.
Tap the mic. Say the 3 pairs. Tap again. Listen.
Check: can short? Can't long?
speaking.tutor: Say ten lines to the tutor, some with can and some with can't, in any order. Ask it which ones it heard as can't, and check against your list.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Music and films
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Music? Films? B: I like music and films.
2. A: Cooking? B: I love cooking.
3. A: Running? B: I don't like running.
4. A: Swimming? Singing? B: I like swimming and singing.
5. A: What is your favourite game? B: My favourite game is football.
Tap the mic. Say the 5 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Now say them for you. Change the words. True or made up is fine.
Check: -ing after like and love? And in 1 and 4?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name two things at a time, like music and football. Answer each with like, love, don't like or hate, and join the two with and.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — At the sports centre desk
speaking.instructions:
You are at the desk of a sports centre.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! What is your name, please?
You: Hello. My name is ___.
Desk: Can you swim?
You: Yes, I can. Or: No, I can't.
Desk: What can you do?
You: I can ___ and ___.
Desk: What is your favourite game?
You: My favourite game is ___.
Desk: Thanks. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name. Your answers can be made up.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? Can or can't in line 2? And in line 3?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
You are at the desk of a sports centre.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! What is your name, please?
You: Hello. My name is …
Desk: Can you swim?
You: Yes, I can. Or: No, I can't.
Desk: What can you do?
You: I can … and …
Desk: What is your favourite game?
You: My favourite game is …
Desk: Thanks. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name. Your answers can be made up.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? Can or can't in line 2? And in line 3?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be the person at the sports centre desk and ask the four questions. Your answers can be made up.

writing.title: Writing 1 — I can, I can't
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines.
Say what you can do and what you can't do.
They can be true or made up.
writing.model:
I can cook.
I can draw.
I can't drive.
I can't sing.
writing.criteria:
4 lines.
2 lines with can. 2 lines with can't.
No -ing and no to after can.
A capital letter and a full stop (.) in each.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change only the last word in each line.
Pick from: swim, cook, draw, dance, sing, drive.
writing.extension: Join two lines with and: I can cook and I can ride a bike.

writing.title: Writing 2 — What I like
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines with love, like, don't like and hate.
Put a word with -ing in each line.
They can be true or made up.
writing.model:
I love dancing.
I like cooking.
I don't like running.
I hate driving.
writing.criteria:
4 lines: love, like, don't like, hate.
A word with -ing in each line.
Spelling: dancing has no e. Swimming has two m. Running has two n.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the -ing word only.
Check each one with the list in Pattern 2.
writing.extension: Add a line with and: I like cooking and singing.

writing.title: Writing 3 — Two things with and
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines about you with and.
In 2 lines, join two words.
In 2 lines, join two parts with I can or I like.
writing.model:
I like music and films.
I can sing and dance.
I can cook and I can drive.
I like walking and I love swimming.
writing.criteria:
4 lines, each with and.
One full stop in each line, at the end.
After like and love: -ing on both words.
writing.support:
Start with two short lines: I can sing. I can dance.
Now put and between them.
I can sing and I can dance.
writing.extension: Write one line with three things: I can sing, dance and draw.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A card for a group
writing.prompt:
Write a card for a free-time group.
The group is at a library or a sports centre.
You can use a made-up name.
Your answers can be made up.
writing.model:
FREE-TIME GROUP
Name: Tomas
I can: swim and ride a bike
I can't: sing
I like: football and music
My favourite: football
writing.criteria:
5 lines: name, I can, I can't, I like, my favourite.
And in 2 lines.
Spell these right: can't, favourite and each -ing word.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change one word in each line.
Check favourite: f-a-v-o-u-r-i-t-e.
writing.extension: Write 2 lines under the card: I can … and … . I like … and … .

activities.title: Practice 1 — Can or can't
activities.instructions:
Read. Then write can or can't.
Priya: cook, yes. Drive, yes. Swim, no. Sing, no.
Tomas: swim, yes. Dance, yes. Cook, no. Drive, no.
1. Priya ___ cook.
2. Priya ___ swim.
3. Tomas ___ swim.
4. Tomas ___ drive.
5. Priya ___ drive.
6. Tomas ___ cook.
7. Tomas ___ dance.
8. Priya ___ sing.
activities.answers:
1. can  2. can't  3. can  4. can't  5. can  6. can't  7. can  8. can't
Check 2 and 3: swim is no for Priya and yes for Tomas.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Add -ing
activities.instructions:
Write the word with -ing.
1. cook
2. swim
3. dance
4. walk
5. run
6. ride
7. play
8. sleep
9. carry
10. speak
activities.answers:
1. cooking  2. swimming  3. dancing  4. walking  5. running  6. riding  7. playing  8. sleeping  9. carrying  10. speaking
The hard ones: 2 and 5 (two m, two n), 3 and 6 (drop the e).
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each word out loud. Write it. Check each letter with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Can swim, like swimming
activities.instructions:
Write the right word.
1. I can (swim / swimming).
2. I like (cook / cooking).
3. I can't (drive / driving).
4. I love (dance / dancing).
5. Can you (sing / singing)?
6. I don't like (run / running).
7. I hate (carry / carrying) bags.
8. I can (ride / riding) a bike.
activities.answers:
1. swim  2. cooking  3. drive  4. dancing  5. sing  6. running  7. carrying  8. ride
The rule: can and can't, no -ing. Like, love, don't like and hate, -ing.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Patterns 1 and 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud with your word. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Join with and
activities.instructions:
Make one line with and.
1. I can swim. I can run.
2. I like football. I like music.
3. Ana can cook. Lena can cook.
4. I love singing. I love dancing.
5. I can draw. I can count to twenty.
6. I like films. I like songs. I like games.
activities.answers:
1. I can swim and I can run. Or: I can swim and run.
2. I like football and music. Or: I like football and I like music.
3. Ana and Lena can cook.
4. I love singing and dancing. Or: I love singing and I love dancing.
5. I can draw and I can count to twenty. Or: I can draw and count to twenty.
6. I like films, songs and games.
Wrong on 6? Three things: a comma, then and.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each line. Read it out loud. Check with the key. Both answers count where the key gives two.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Match the word
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 8 with a to h.
1. football
2. song
3. bike
4. film
5. TV
6. favourite
7. language
8. hate
a. You sing it.
b. You ride it.
c. A game with a ball.
d. The one you like the most.
e. It is at home. Films are on it.
f. Not like at all.
g. A long story you look at.
h. English is one.
activities.answers:
1c  2a  3b  4g  5e  6d  7h  8f
Check 4 and 5: a film is the story. The TV is the thing at home.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: go back to Words, listen again, and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each word out loud. Write the letter. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Make the sentence
activities.instructions:
Make a sentence.
Start with a capital letter.
End with a full stop or ?
1. can / I / swim
2. like / I / cooking
3. you / can / drive
4. don't / I / running / like
5. and / sing / I / dance / can
6. is / favourite / my / football / game
7. can / speak / Yara / two languages
activities.answers:
1. I can swim.
2. I like cooking.
3. Can you drive?
4. I don't like running.
5. I can sing and dance.
6. My favourite game is football.
7. Yara can speak two languages.
Number 3: a question starts with Can. Can you drive?
Number 6: Football is my favourite game. That is right too.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Patterns 1 to 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each sentence. Read it out loud. Check with the key.

quizzes.why: Yes: can. Can't is no. Can has no s, so not cans. Like needs -ing: like driving.
After can, the word stays the same: I can swim. Not to swim. Not swimming. Swims has an s. No s after can.
After like, add -ing: I like cooking. I like cook has no -ing. Can cook and am cook do not go after like.
After love, add -ing. Dance ends in e, so drop the e: dancing. Danceing keeps the e. Dance and dances have no -ing.
Swim takes two m: swimming. Swiming has one m. To swimming is not right. Swim has no -ing.
A question with can gets can in the answer. No goes with can't. No, I can says no and yes. Don't and am do not answer a can question.

quizzes.q: I can sing. I can dance. Which one line is right?
options: I can sing, I can dance.
quizzes.why: And joins them: I can sing and dance. A comma alone does not join two lines. After can, no -ing. And goes between the two words.

quizzes.q: Three things: sing, dance, draw. Which is right?
options: I can sing and dance draw.
I can sing, dance and draw.
I can and sing dance draw.
quizzes.a: I can sing, dance and draw.
quizzes.why: Three things: a comma, then and before the last one. Sing, dance, draw has no and. And goes before draw, not after can.
After like, both words take -ing: cooking and swimming. Swim and swims have no -ing. Can swim does not go after like.

quizzes.q: The one you like the most is your ___.
quizzes.why: Favourite: your number one. Love is a thing you do: I love music. A language is words people speak. Hate is not like at all.
You ride a bike. You sing a song. A TV is at home, with films on it. English is a language you speak.

quizzes.q: A sign says: No running. Which one is OK?
quizzes.why: No running means do not run. So walk. Run is the thing the sign says no to. Ride a bike and sleep are not on the sign.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a short checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together and point at the checklist rather than correcting mid-sentence.

teacherNotes.type: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: The two patterns meet in this unit, so they swap: I can swimming, I like cook. Practice 3 sets them side by side on purpose. When you hear one, point at the word before the verb, can or like, and let the learner fix the verb themselves. The tip line is the whole rule: can swim, like swimming.

No task asks whether the learner can really swim, drive or ride a bike. Every I can task lets them pick or invent, and a made-up answer practises the language exactly as well as a true one. Driving in particular depends on age and on where a person lives; never ask, and never correct a made-up answer.

I don't like is used as one chunk with like. Questions and short answers with do, and short forms such as don't and isn't, are Unit 7, so do not explain do here. Every question here is built with can or with is, so none needs do. He likes, with its s, is also left for later: this unit keeps like to I, you, we and they, and teaches only that can has no s. Joining with but, or and then is Unit 13.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. The learner is told throughout that a made-up name and made-up answers are fine. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real personal details.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say what I can do and can't do.
I can write: I like cooking. I don't like running.
I can say two things with and.
I can answer: Can you swim? Yes, I can.
I can read what people can do and like.
I can write a card with can, like and and.

assignment.title: I can, I like
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say hello and your name. Say two things you can do and one thing you can't do. Say two things you like, with and. Say goodbye.
2. Write a group card like Writing 4.
You can use a made-up name. Your answers can be made up.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written card
